blocks.content: The primary objectives of FCI are safeguarding the interests of farmers through MSP, distributing foodgrains for vulnerable sections, and maintaining buffer stocks for national food security.

rows: Ensure food security for vulnerable sections
PDS / NFSA beneficiaries via Fair Price Shops
National reserves managed via FCI & CWC warehouses

items: FCI was set up under the Food Corporations Act, 1964 and commenced operations in 1965 with headquarters initially in Chennai (later moved to New Delhi).
MSP is recommended by CACP (Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices), but procurement operations are executed by FCI along with state agencies.
Buffer stock norms are fixed quarterly (1st January, 1st April, 1st July, and 1st October) by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Effective price support operations for safeguarding the interests of the farmers through Minimum Support Price (MSP).
Distribution of foodgrains throughout the country for the Public Distribution System (PDS) and National Food Security Act (NFSA).
Maintaining satisfactory levels of operational and buffer stocks of foodgrains to ensure national food security.
Intervention in the open market through Open Market Sale Scheme (OMSS) for price stabilization during lean seasons.
